notes.problem: A generic CG dais: empty navy wall over procedural orange wood, no window source or nameplate in frame.
notes.fix: Put the window in frame at left as the single visible source, crop the wall to a band so the case and a nameplate fill the lower half, and let the wood outside the pool fall to black.

notes.problem: Bottom 45 percent is mid-tone orange procedural wood. The back wall is flat navy that reads as sky, not a room. No window is in frame, the nameplates are missing and the shut case reads as a laptop, so the frame fails 'a room is dark around one source'.
notes.fix: Push the camera in to ledge height (eye 0.9 m, fov 30) so the case fills a third of the width, kill the room fill so the dais front falls to near black, and light only a narrow window shaft from the left across the lid and brass latch, with the window frame visible top left.

notes.problem: Generic CG dais with a shut box. Warm walnut fills the lower half in mid tones under a flat navy wall, and nothing in the image shows 'approved but still a draft', so the frame explains nothing at feed size.
notes.fix: Open the case on the ledge so the brass and blued weights show, lay an unbound minutes sheet beside it under the raking window key, and crop tight at ledge height so case and sheet own half the frame. Let the light fall off to black on the wall rather than lighting the navy.

notes.problem: A flat grey sheet under a dead band, a hard seam with a notch near x 800 (the bootFlat artifact), and a coin-like weight.
notes.fix: Raise the relief so the sheet starts under the dek and the seam leaves the frame; stand the chassis slotted weight on row (f) at a low oblique.

notes.problem: Top 45 percent is dead black over a hard step seam (native about y 1350, step at x 1080). The pooled grey sheet is a flat mid band and the weight reads as a Q-shaped coin.
notes.fix: Re-shoot as an oblique txthree view at elevation 13 so the agenda leaf recedes into the dark, with the pool only on row (f) and the knurled stack-style weight standing on it. Remove the wash/tile seam so the board falls off continuously.

notes.problem: Flat grey sheet over the right two thirds with a hard vertical seam against the pecan strip and a dead black band under the dek. The single weight reads as a button seen from above. It is the deck's one mid-grey frame.
notes.fix: Re-shoot the sheet as a low oblique txthree camera so the slotted weight stands as a tall brass cylinder casting a long shadow across the consent rows. Bleed the sheet off both sides to remove the seam, and pool the key on row (f) so the paper falls to dark.

notes.problem: Cracks read as paving, the same seam artifact, and a dead top 45 percent.
notes.fix: Move the board up to span y 700 to 1800 and use sparse hairline shrink swell cracks.

notes.problem: A grey board with vector-looking Voronoi hairlines and a rectangular notch artifact (native about x 0 to 1080, y 1190 to 1350) reads as a UI progress bar. The discs barely stand proud.
notes.fix: Lay the two rows in grooves on the dark chalk plinth at a low three-quarter txthree camera, with the key raking along the grooves so each disc casts. Extend the board's falloff across the full width to remove the notch.

notes.problem: Two thin rows of small discs across the lower half of a cracked clay board with the upper 45 percent empty, so the turn frame reads as a flat striped bar chart.
notes.fix: Drop the camera to a low oblique looking along the grooves so the discs stand as receding cylinders. Fill about 60 percent of the frame height, with the four empty blued wells lit in the foreground as the focal point.

notes.problem: Near repeat of slide 1's camera; both pan strings cross the type and the brass stack sits against 'c1'.
notes.fix: Build the planned level macro on the needle and arc with the pillar cut by the bottom edge, so no stirrup or stack enters the type bands.

notes.problem: 01's camera repeated. The needle renders as a flat grey plank, the dark arc's graduations are unreadable, and a DOM leader and white dot carry the reading.
notes.fix: Build the planned macro with the pillar moved out of frame to the left: camera level with the arc at 0.30 m, a nickel BRDF on the needle with the key down its bevel, and a lit brass index under the tip. Then drop the DOM dot and leader.

notes.problem: Near repeat of 01's camera. Pans and stacks are cut by the bottom edge under the footer, the arc carries no visible graduations, and the floating mono label does the work the image should.
notes.fix: Build the planned macro with the pillar pushed off frame left and the camera level with the arc at 0.3 m, so the needle tip on its index and the engraved graduations fill the lower half. Otherwise cut the frame, as the one sentence fix proposes.

notes.problem: Blued reads lilac, only about 13 of 15 discs clear the pan rim, and a dark bar sits behind the dek at x 0 to 585, y 1305 to 1480.
notes.fix: Lower the camera so all 15 discs stand above the rim, delete the bar object, and pull the blued toward #4E5FA8.

notes.problem: The balance is a thin linework silhouette with little mass. The plinth face is a flat taupe band under the source line, the needle is the same grey plank, and the chamber glazing is cool navy, so the declared warm seam is absent.
notes.fix: Move the camera to 1.0 m at fov 24 so the beam spans about 80 percent of the width and the stacks gain mass, warm the city hall glazing into a seam behind the beam, and let the plinth face fall out of the pool to black.

notes.problem: The knurl reads as barcode bars on the shadow side, and the headline sits on a darkening wash plate over the flat taupe plinth.
notes.fix: Replace the knurl geometry with a fine normal map so the shadow side falls to black, and drop the plinth out of the key pool so the type sits on true dark without a plate.
